mike.k: Heads-up — planning schema change tonight 02:00 UTC. Add partial index on events(created_at) + backfill ~3M rows. Plan: canary (1%) -> full. Expect backfill to run in batches, ~30m total. Could see short row-level locks per batch, but want to be cautious. Release notes: https://go/release/12345
irene.db: Concern — our nightly full backup runs 02:00–03:00 UTC on primary. If a backfill causes long locks we could cause backup failures. Recommend quiesce replica traffic, add a safepoint, and run backfill with conservative params: batch_size=1k, throttle=500ms. Also prefer staged rollout with explicit holdpoints.
sam-oncall: +1 on conservative params. I'll monitor pg_locks and the lock-time histogram. Can we add an automated abort if avg lock > 2s for a few checks?
deploy-bot: Scheduled job created: release-12345 job jb_7782 at 2024-03-01T02:00:00Z by mike.k. Use `/deploy cancel jb_7782` to abort.
mike.k: Added an automated abort hook — rollout will cancel if avg_lock_ms > 2000 for 3 consecutive checks. Updated rollout config:
```
batch_size: 1000
throttle_ms: 500
canary_pct: 1
abort_on_lock_ms: 2000
```
dave.sql: We also have a long-running analytics aggregate that starts ~02:30 and will overlap with the tail of the backfill. I'd prefer we move to tomorrow's maintenance window (2024-03-02 01:00 UTC) to avoid any overlap.
mike.k: Makes sense. Moving the run. @deploy-bot please reschedule jb_7782 to 2024-03-02T01:00:00Z and pin migration to release-12345-v2 to prevent concurrent migrations. Also adding note in the ops channel.
deploy-bot: Job jb_7782 rescheduled to 2024-03-02T01:00:00Z by mike.k. Reason: backup_conflict / analytics overlap. Link: https://go/deploys/jb_7782/logs
anna-eng: Thanks — I'll update the release notes and the ops runbook. Escape hatch SQL for abort is: `UPDATE feature_flags SET value='off' WHERE name='events_partial_index_backfill';` Runbook: https://go/runbooks/backfill-abort
sam-oncall: I'll be on watch for the new window. If locks exceed thresholds we'll trigger the abort. :thumbsup:
